source: A1 Kiswahili for Beginners by Yunia

words.definition: A common greeting used to ask how someone is doing
words.example: Habari ya asubuhi! - Good morning!

words.definition: A casual greeting used with strangers or tourists
words.example: Jambo! - Hello!

words.definition: A respectful greeting used when addressing elders
words.example: Shikamoo Mwalimu. - Greetings, Teacher.

words.definition: The standard response when someone greets you with Shikamoo
words.example: Shikamoo. Marahaba. - Greetings. I acknowledge you.

words.definition: The period of the day from sunrise to noon
words.example: Habari ya asubuhi! - Good morning!

words.definition: The period of the day from noon to evening
words.example: Habari ya mchana! - Good afternoon!

words.definition: The period of the day from late afternoon to night
words.example: Habari ya jioni! - Good evening!

words.definition: The period of darkness between evening and morning
words.example: Usiku mwema! - Good night!

words.definition: Used to express that something is good or that one is well
words.example: Habari? Nzuri. - How are you? Fine.

words.definition: An intensifier meaning very or a lot
words.example: Asante sana! - Thank you very much!

words.definition: Expression of gratitude
words.example: Asante sana! - Thank you very much!

words.definition: A polite word used when making a request
words.example: Tafadhali nisaidie. - Please help me.

words.definition: Used to apologise or to get someone's attention politely
words.example: Samahani, uko wapi? - Excuse me, where are you?

words.definition: An expression of sympathy or apology
words.example: Pole sana. - I am very sorry.

words.definition: A farewell greeting used when parting
words.example: Kwaheri! Tutaonana kesho. - Goodbye! We will see each other tomorrow.

words.definition: The word or words by which a person or thing is known
words.example: Jina langu ni Maria. - My name is Maria.

words.definition: First person singular personal pronoun
words.example: Mimi ni mwanafunzi. - I am a student.

words.definition: Second person singular personal pronoun
words.example: Wewe unatoka wapi? - Where are you from?

words.definition: Third person singular personal pronoun
words.example: Yeye ni mwalimu. - He/She is a teacher.

words.definition: First person plural personal pronoun
words.example: Sisi tunaishi Nairobi. - We live in Nairobi.

words.definition: Second person plural personal pronoun
words.example: Nyinyi mnatoka wapi? - Where do you all come from?

words.definition: Third person plural personal pronoun
words.example: Wao ni wanafunzi. - They are students.

words.definition: An affirmative reply
words.example: Je, unajua Kiswahili? Ndiyo. - Do you know Swahili? Yes.

words.definition: A negative reply
words.example: Je, una pesa? Hapana. - Do you have money? No.

words.definition: A person with whom one has a bond of mutual affection
words.example: Yeye ni rafiki yangu. - He/She is my friend.

words.definition: A person who teaches, especially in a school
words.example: Mwalimu anafundisha darasani. - The teacher teaches in the classroom.

words.definition: A person who is studying at a school or university
words.example: Mimi ni mwanafunzi. - I am a student.

words.definition: Used to indicate origin or starting point
words.example: Ninatoka Kenya. - I am from Kenya.

words.definition: A question word asking about location
words.example: Unakaa wapi? - Where do you live?

words.definition: A large group of people sharing the same history, culture or language
words.example: Kenya ni taifa kubwa. - Kenya is a great nation.

words.definition: A nation with its own government and territory
words.example: Unatoka nchi gani? - What country are you from?

words.definition: A large or important settlement
words.example: Ninaishi mjini Nairobi. - I live in the city of Nairobi.

words.definition: A small settlement in a rural area
words.example: Yeye anaishi kijijini. - He/She lives in a village.

words.definition: In, at, or to this place or position
words.example: Ninaishi hapa. - I live here.

words.definition: In, at, or to that place
words.example: Tukae pale. - Let us sit there.

words.definition: A male parent
words.example: Baba yangu anafanya kazi. - My father is working.

words.definition: A female parent
words.example: Mama yangu anapika chakula. - My mother is cooking food.

words.definition: A male sibling
words.example: Kaka yangu anasoma. - My brother is studying.

words.definition: A female sibling
words.example: Dada yangu ni mwanafunzi. - My sister is a student.

words.definition: A young human being
words.example: Mtoto anacheza. - The child is playing.

words.definition: The mother of one's parent
words.example: Nyanya yangu anaishi kijijini. - My grandmother lives in a village.

words.definition: The father of one's parent
words.example: Babu yangu ni mzee. - My grandfather is old.

words.definition: The brother of one's mother
words.example: Mjomba wangu anaishi Mombasa. - My uncle lives in Mombasa.

words.definition: The sister of one's father
words.example: Shangazi yangu ni mwalimu. - My aunt is a teacher.

words.definition: A married man in relation to his wife
words.example: Mume wake anafanya kazi. - Her husband is working.

words.definition: A married woman in relation to her husband
words.example: Mke wake ni daktari. - His wife is a doctor.

words.definition: A child of one's uncle or aunt
words.example: Binamu yangu anaishi Kisumu. - My cousin lives in Kisumu.

words.definition: Rice that has been boiled and is ready to eat
words.example: Ninapenda wali na samaki. - I like rice with fish.

words.definition: A staple food made from maize flour cooked in water to a stiff consistency
words.example: Ugali na nyama ni chakula kizuri. - Ugali with meat is good food.

words.definition: A domestic bird kept for its eggs and meat
words.example: Ninataka kuku na wali. - I want chicken and rice.

words.definition: Animal flesh used as food
words.example: Nyama choma ni tamu sana. - Roasted meat is very delicious.

words.definition: An aquatic animal used as food
words.example: Napenda samaki wa kukaanga. - I like fried fish.

words.definition: Seeds used as a food vegetable
words.example: Maharagwe ni chakula cha bei nafuu. - Beans are an affordable food.

words.definition: Plants or parts of plants used as food
words.example: Kula mboga ni afya nzuri. - Eating vegetables is good health.

words.definition: A starchy plant tuber used as food
words.example: Ninataka viazi na kuku. - I want potatoes and chicken.

words.definition: A thin flat unleavened bread cooked on a griddle, common in East Africa
words.example: Chapati na chai ni kifungua kinywa kizuri. - Flatbread and tea is a good breakfast.

words.definition: A dish of rice cooked with spices and usually meat
words.example: Pilau ni chakula tamu sana. - Spiced rice is very delicious food.

words.definition: A clear liquid essential for life
words.example: Ninataka maji baridi. - I want cold water.

words.definition: A hot drink made by infusing tea leaves in water
words.example: Ninapenda chai ya maziwa. - I like milk tea.

words.definition: A drink made from roasted coffee beans
words.example: Kahawa ya Kenya ni nzuri sana. - Kenyan coffee is very good.

words.definition: A white liquid produced by mammals used as food
words.example: Mtoto anapenda maziwa. - The child likes milk.

words.definition: A sweet crystalline substance used to sweeten food and drinks
words.example: Ninataka sukari kidogo. - I want a little sugar.

words.definition: A white crystalline substance used to season food
words.example: Ongeza chumvi kidogo. - Add a little salt.

words.definition: The edible product of a plant
words.example: Napenda kula matunda. - I like eating fruits.

words.definition: A long curved fruit with yellow skin when ripe
words.example: Ndizi ni matunda mazuri. - Bananas are good fruits.

words.definition: A large tropical fruit with a sweet yellow flesh
words.example: Embe la Kenya ni tamu sana. - Kenyan mango is very sweet.

words.definition: The star at the centre of our solar system
words.example: Leo jua ni kali. - Today the sun is intense.

words.definition: Water that falls from clouds
words.example: Mvua inanyesha. - It is raining.

words.definition: Moving air, especially a strong current of air
words.example: Upepo mkali unakuja. - Strong wind is coming.

words.definition: High temperature or the condition of being warm
words.example: Leo ni joto sana. - Today it is very hot.

words.definition: Low temperature or the sensation of low temperature
words.example: Maji ni baridi sana. - The water is very cold.

words.definition: Frozen water vapour that falls as white flakes
words.example: Milima ina theluji. - The mountains have snow.

words.definition: A violent disturbance of weather with strong winds and rain
words.example: Dhoruba kubwa inakuja. - A big storm is coming.

words.definition: The amount of money expected in exchange for something
words.example: Bei yake ni ngapi? - What is its price?

words.definition: Costing a lot of money
words.example: Nyama ni ghali sana. - Meat is very expensive.

words.definition: Low in price or cost
words.example: Maharagwe ni nafuu. - Beans are cheap.

words.definition: A medium of exchange used to buy goods and services
words.example: Una pesa ngapi? - How much money do you have?

words.definition: The currency unit used in Kenya, Tanzania and other East African countries
words.example: Ninataka shilingi mia moja. - I want one hundred shillings.

words.definition: A building or room where goods are sold
words.example: Ninaenda dukani. - I am going to the shop.

words.definition: A place where people buy and sell goods
words.example: Mama anaenda sokoni. - Mother is going to the market.

words.definition: The property of an object seen as a result of light reflection
words.example: Rangi gani unayopenda? - What colour do you like?

words.definition: The colour of snow or milk
words.example: Nguo yangu ni nyeupe. - My clothes are white.

words.definition: The darkest colour, the opposite of white
words.example: Gari lake ni nyeusi. - His car is black.

words.definition: The colour of blood or fire
words.example: Tofaa nyekundu ni tamu. - Red apples are sweet.

words.definition: The colour of grass and leaves
words.example: Mboga ni kijani. - Vegetables are green.

words.definition: The colour of the sun or ripe bananas
words.example: Ndizi ni njano. - Bananas are yellow.

words.definition: A dark orange-red colour like earth or wood
words.example: Ardhi ni kahawia. - The soil is brown.

words.definition: Of a large size or extent
words.example: Nyumba yake ni kubwa sana. - His house is very big.

words.definition: Of a small size or extent
words.example: Mtoto ni mdogo. - The child is small.

words.definition: A wide path for vehicles and people to travel on
words.example: Barabara ni ndefu. - The road is long.

words.definition: A route or track along which someone or something moves
words.example: Njia hii inaenda wapi? - Where does this path go?

words.definition: The direction to the left side of the body
words.example: Geuka kushoto. - Turn left.

words.definition: The direction to the right side of the body
words.example: Geuka kulia. - Turn right.

words.definition: In front of or in the direction one is facing
words.example: Nenda mbele. - Go straight.

words.definition: At or to the rear
words.example: Nyumba iko nyuma. - The house is behind.

words.definition: Close in distance, or used as an expression of welcome
words.example: Karibu nyumbani! - Welcome home!

words.definition: At a great distance
words.example: Hospitali iko mbali. - The hospital is far.

words.definition: A road vehicle powered by an engine
words.example: Gari lake ni jipya. - His car is new.

words.definition: A car available for hire with a driver
words.example: Nitapanda teksi. - I will take a taxi.

words.definition: A person who drives a vehicle
words.example: Dereva anaendesha gari polepole. - The driver drives the car slowly.

words.definition: A trip or journey, especially one involving travel
words.example: Safari njema! - Have a good journey!

words.definition: A card or paper that gives the right to travel or enter somewhere
words.example: Ninataka tiketi moja. - I want one ticket.

words.definition: The money charged for a journey by bus, taxi or other transport
words.example: Nauli ni shilingi ngapi? - How much is the fare?

words.definition: At a fast speed
words.example: Nenda haraka! - Go quickly!

words.definition: At a slow speed
words.example: Endesha polepole. - Drive slowly.

words.definition: A period of time equal to sixty seconds
words.example: Subiri dakika moja. - Wait one minute.

words.definition: A period of sixty minutes, or the measurement of time
words.example: Saa ngapi sasa? - What time is it now?

words.definition: On the current day
words.example: Leo ni Jumatatu. - Today is Monday.

words.definition: The day after today
words.example: Tutaonana kesho. - We will see each other tomorrow.

words.definition: Activity involving effort done to achieve a purpose
words.example: Ninakwenda kazini. - I am going to work.

words.definition: The activity of reading or learning from books or lessons
words.example: Ninapenda kusoma vitabu. - I like reading books.

words.definition: To put food into the mouth and swallow it
words.example: Ninataka kula sasa. - I want to eat now.

words.definition: To be in a state of rest with eyes closed
words.example: Mtoto analala. - The child is sleeping.

words.definition: To wash oneself with water
words.example: Ninaoga kila asubuhi. - I bathe every morning.

words.definition: Any substance that people eat or drink to maintain life
words.example: Chakula kiko tayari. - The food is ready.

words.definition: A building for human habitation
words.example: Nyumba yake ni kubwa. - His house is big.

words.definition: An institution for educating children
words.example: Watoto wanaenda shuleni. - The children are going to school.

words.definition: A place where sick or injured people are treated
words.example: Daktari anafanya kazi hospitalini. - The doctor works at the hospital.

words.definition: A person qualified to treat people who are ill or injured
words.example: Daktari anamsaidia mgonjwa. - The doctor is helping the patient.

words.definition: A group of people related by blood or marriage
words.example: Familia yangu ni kubwa. - My family is big.

words.definition: A person who lives next door or nearby
words.example: Jirani yangu ni rafiki yangu. - My neighbour is my friend.

words.definition: A room or building used for work
words.example: Ninaenda ofisini. - I am going to the office.

words.definition: A financial institution that keeps and lends money
words.example: Ninaenda benki kupata pesa. - I am going to the bank to get money.

words.definition: A diagram representing an area showing features such as roads and rivers
words.example: Una ramani ya mji? - Do you have a map of the city?

words.definition: A person who works on a farm growing crops or raising animals
words.example: Mkulima analima shamba. - The farmer is cultivating the farm.

words.definition: A skilled worker or artisan
words.example: Fundi anarekebisha gari. - The technician is fixing the car.

words.definition: An official body responsible for maintaining law and order
words.example: Polisi anasaidia watu. - The police officer is helping people.

words.definition: Free from dirt or other unwanted substances
words.example: Nyumba ni safi sana. - The house is very clean.

words.definition: Used to express agreement or that something is acceptable
words.example: Sawa, tutaonana kesho. - Okay, we will see each other tomorrow.

words.definition: A question word asking about time
words.example: Unakuja lini? - When are you coming?

words.definition: A question word asking about a person
words.example: Yeye ni nani? - Who is he/she?

words.definition: A question word asking about type or kind
words.example: Unataka chakula gani? - What food do you want?

words.definition: A question word asking about quantity or number
words.example: Una watoto wangapi? - How many children do you have?

words.definition: At a time in the future
words.example: Tutaonana baadaye. - We will see each other later.

words.definition: Before the expected or usual time
words.example: Niamke mapema. - Wake me up early.

words.definition: To stay in place until something expected happens
words.example: Subiri hapa. - Wait here.

words.definition: To reach a destination
words.example: Tutafika saa ngapi? - What time will we arrive?

words.definition: To cease moving or operating
words.example: Simama hapa! - Stop here!

words.definition: To move from one place to another
words.example: Nenda shuleni. - Go to school.

words.definition: To go back to a place or person
words.example: Rudi nyumbani mapema. - Return home early.

words.definition: To change direction
words.example: Geuka kulia pale. - Turn right there.

words.definition: To go across from one side to another
words.example: Vuka barabara kwa uangalifu. - Cross the road carefully.

words.definition: To climb or get onto a vehicle
words.example: Panda basi hapa. - Board the bus here.

words.definition: To descend or exit a vehicle
words.example: Shuka hapa. - Get off here.

words.definition: A place where buses or trains stop regularly
words.example: Kituo cha basi kiko mbali. - The bus station is far.

words.definition: To emerge from sleep
words.example: Ninaamka saa moja asubuhi. - I wake up at seven in the morning.

words.definition: Physical activity done to keep the body healthy
words.example: Ninafanya mazoezi kila asubuhi. - I exercise every morning.

words.definition: A device for receiving and displaying broadcast images and sound
words.example: Ninaangalia televisheni jioni. - I watch television in the evening.

words.definition: A food made from flour, water and usually yeast
words.example: Ninataka mkate na siagi. - I want bread and butter.

words.definition: Oval objects laid by female birds, used as food
words.example: Ninapenda mayai ya kuchemsha. - I like boiled eggs.

words.definition: Air moving horizontally
words.example: Upepo mkali unakuja pwani. - Strong wind is coming from the coast.

words.definition: A long period of little or no rainfall
words.example: Ukame umesababisha njaa. - Drought has caused hunger.

words.definition: A visible mass of water droplets in the sky
words.example: Mawingu mengi yanakuja. - Many clouds are coming.

words.definition: Substances used to flavour food
words.example: Pilau inahitaji viungo vingi. - Spiced rice needs many spices.

words.definition: Having a pleasant flavour
words.example: Chakula hiki ni tamu sana. - This food is very delicious.

words.definition: A sweet baked food made from flour, eggs and sugar
words.example: Keki ya siku ya kuzaliwa ni tamu. - Birthday cake is sweet.

words.definition: A liquid dish made by boiling meat or vegetables in water
words.example: Supu ya kuku ni nzuri sana. - Chicken soup is very good.

words.definition: A dish of raw vegetables
words.example: Ninataka saladi na chakula changu. - I want salad with my food.
